transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Petra 3 FP, Anselm 3 FP, Caddock 3 FP, Yarrow 3 FP. Face-up: The Hive Blight [H-02], Hollowmoot [L-03].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain hammers the plank-walks of Hollowmoot as your boat bumps against a mooring post slick with algae. The market's still open despite the weather — oilcloth stalls, fish-gutters, a Warden with a torch eyeing every stranger's hands for wounds. Somewhere above the gutter-hiss, a bell rings twice, short and sharp: the quarantine signal, though no smoke rises yet. Gossip moves faster than the floodwater here, and half of it is about you before you've even tied off the rope.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: The song's not random—it's got a rhythm, a direction. If I can read it, we might know where it's going before the Wardens do.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra pushes through the rain-slick crowd toward the Warden, her attention sharpening on the sound beneath the bells and the gutter-hiss. She's listening for the swarm-song, that strange harmonic only she hears clearly. Her shoulders tense as she tracks where it's strongest, where the hive-touched might already be moving through the stilt-town's channels.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: The quarantine bells—that's new. Or maybe I've just been gone too long to remember how often they ring these days. I know half the gossip in this town before breakfast.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm ties off the boat rope with practiced efficiency and steps onto the wet plank-walk, taking in the market's pulse. He pulls his cloak tighter against the rain and scans for the familiar faces—the mill-folk he's known since childhood, the Warden's bearing and how the stall-keepers are keeping their distance from the watch. Before he moves deeper into the crowd, he marks the Warden's position and the path toward the taverns where real information trades. He's home, and home is dangerous right now.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: The bell's rung twice. What's the count? I may have work to do here.

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock approaches the Warden at the gate with professional bearing, hands visible, satchel on display. She addresses him as one practitioner to another, asking about the quarantine situation with the directness of someone who deals with emergencies.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: That bell, and the way he's watching hands—the Hive Blight's spreading again. We move careful through here, show empty sleeves, stick together. I'll get us past the gate.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow secures the boat's rope and looks up at the bell tower, then back toward the Warden by the gate. His hand stays on the coil of rope—not hostile, but ready. He turns to the others and keeps his voice low, nodding toward the inspector watching for wounds. The quarantine bell means something has the Wardens spooked. He positions himself between the group and the Warden, a disgraced guard still holding the line.)

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: No—no, wait, that's not... the song knows me. The song *knows* me.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra — create advantage with Notice: dice + 0 - 0 → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Petra shoulders past a fish-gutter's cart, eyes half-closed, and for a moment the swarm-song rises clear above the bell and rain — and inside it, unmistakably, her own name. She stumbles, one hand catching a post, the old fear of PE-03's freezing grip closing her throat for a heartbeat before she wrenches free of it. But the freeze cost her nothing this time: she reads the pattern clean, tracing the harmonic's pull like a compass needle swinging south toward the water-stairs and the old temple road. She calls it back to the others — "It's moving. Whatever's calling, it wants us at the stairs, not the market" — and the words settle over the group as a shared certainty: *Reading the Blight's Spread in the Swarm-Song* now marks the way the hive-touched are drifting through Hollowmoot's flooded lanes. The Warden at the gate doesn't miss her stagger, though — his torch dips half an inch lower, tracking her hands for wounds.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: The quarantine bell rang twice. I know what's calling—it's moving toward the water-stairs right now, and we need to get there first, not stand here.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra turns to face the Warden head-on, both hands open and visible, no flinching from his torch-light. There's no apology in her stare—just the absolute certainty of someone who's heard something in the swarm-song that matters more than his suspicion. She steps toward the gate with intention, the way someone moves when they know the ground beneath them is about to give way and there's no time left to ask nicely.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: The bells ran twice—how far has the Blight gotten this time, Warden? I've been away too long to count the rings myself.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm moves toward the Warden with the practiced ease of someone who belongs in Hollowmoot, positioning himself prominently to draw the watchman's attention away from Petra's earlier stagger. He addresses the Warden directly in the tone of a local catching up on town business, his bearing steady and familiar.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: She's clean, Warden—I've checked her myself, and you know what that means in this town. The bell's twice; births are coming. You want the best midwife in the Sallowmere standing here, or moving up to meet them?

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock steps forward smoothly into the Warden's line of sight, placing herself between him and Petra without hesitation. She meets his eyes with the calm authority of someone who's delivered in plague years, fire-seasons, and worse—her hands stay visible and steady, and she's already mentally moving the group past the gate.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: Easy, Warden. We're through-folk, militia-kin passing to the temple road. Show of hands, yes?—no wounds here. We know the protocols.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow steps forward into the Warden's line of sight with the easy bearing of someone who's stood watch at this gate before, shoulders squared and hands open. He positions himself between the torch and Petra, angling his body so the Warden's attention has to move to him. His voice carries the weight of someone who still remembers how to hold a line, despite everything.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra — overcome with Rapport: dice + 0 - -, invoking Reading the Blight's Spread in the Swarm-Song [A-1.1.1] → Great (+4) vs Great (+4): TIE

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: Your coin, as promised—I'm good for it. Get that hull to dry ground, and come find me when the work is done.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Caddock accepts the compel on 'A Stranded Ferryman'.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The Warden's torch hovers a moment too long, weighing Caddock's word against Petra's stagger — then he grunts and steps aside, waving you all through with a flick of two fingers, as if he's already decided this isn't worth the paperwork. But nothing in Hollowmoot is free: as you pass, a rope-scarred man detaches from the mooring post, the ferryman Caddock swore coin to, and falls into step beside her, reminding her — loudly, so the Warden hears — that a promise made at a gate is a debt owed in daylight. "A Stranded Ferryman" surfaces properly now, PX-01 catching the light of the watchtower lanterns, Caddock's name now tied to his in the town's ledger of favors. You're through the gate and moving toward the water-stairs, Petra's read on the swarm-song still humming true in your ears — but Hollowmoot has marked you, all four, as people worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: An old temple sexton, half-crushed when the nave floor gave way beneath him, drags himself into Hollowmoot on a makeshift crutch — the stones buried three of his fellow pilgrims and he alone crawled free. begs the party to go to He begs you to go to Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple, where the bells still ring out over the flood and pilgrims still answer their call no matter who they bury., because her son followed the swarm-song into the belltower.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The sexton's hands shake as he grips Caddock's sleeve, crutch skidding on the wet planks. "The floor just — opened," he gasps, "swallowed Voss and the Hallet twins whole, and my grandson Tomas ran *toward* the belltower, not away, like the bells were calling only him." Behind him, Hollowmoot's crowd has gone quiet, watching the party with the particular stillness of people deciding whether to blame you for what happens next. Beyond the last stilt-house, the rain-grey shape of Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple broods on the horizon, its belltower the only dry stone left standing, and even from here you can almost hear it: not quite a bell, not quite a voice, singing.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: I hear him calling through the swarm-song — I hear your Tomas. He's not gone yet if I move now. Tell me exactly where the belltower is, and don't hold back on what you saw.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra doesn't wait for permission. She's already pushing past the crowd, grabbing the sexton's arm with one hand while her eyes scan the rain-grey temple on the horizon. She's heard her own name in that song moments ago, and she knows with bone-deep certainty what's calling Tomas into that tower — and what happens if they don't get there first.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: Old man, I've studied Saint Orrin's rites since I was younger than your grandson—if the bells called to him, they called to something in him that might still answer to the old words. Tell me exactly what you heard, and every detail about Tomas before he ran.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm kneels beside the sexton, his eyes sharp with the particular focus of someone who recognizes a thread of his obsession being tugged. He steadies the old man's shaking hand, listening with the intensity of a priest at confession, already weighing what he's heard against everything he knows of Saint Orrin's bell-tongue and the hive's song.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: I know what the song does — I've seen it in Sella's eyes before she was too far gone. Your grandson's still close enough to find if we move now, before the blight takes him deeper into whatever nest grows in that belltower.

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock meets the Sexton's eyes with the same steady certainty she carries into any birthing chamber, no matter the storm outside. She steadies him against her frame, then turns to face the rain-grey shape of the temple on the horizon, already mentally cataloging what she'll need — light, something to break the song's hold, the others at her back.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: I'm going. Tomas didn't have a choice when the bells called him — he needs someone who did and doesn't. Where is the temple, and how do we reach the belltower?

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow steps forward, one hand steadying the sexton by the shoulder. His eyes track across the rain toward the distant belltower, then back to the old man's face. He nods, slow and certain — the gesture of someone who has made a decision and will not unmake it.)

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: Where? Tell me the exact route to that belltower. I hear him in the song and I'm going now.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text:
The sexton's shaking hand rises, finger tracing an invisible path through the rain toward the drowned skyline. "Through the pilgrim's gate — half sunk now — then the nave, if the floor still holds you. The belltower stair is behind the reliquary screen, the only dry climb left in the whole church." His grip tightens on Petra's arm as the swarm-song rises behind his words like a second voice under the first. "I heard your name in it too, girl, before I ran — it knows what it's calling." He can't say more; the debt is paid, the compel taken, Petra's dread of the song a fresh weight she carries now for a fate point earned. Anselm gets the ritual detail he wanted — Tomas cried out something in the old bell-tongue before he ran, words Anselm half-recognizes from his own obsessive study. Caddock reads in the sexton's description of "eyes gone wrong, listening to something else" the same signs she saw in Sella, confirming this is no ordinary panic. Yarrow marks the route in his mind, weir-keeper's instinct for water and stone already plotting the safest line across the flooded approach. As you turn from the sexton toward the temple's grey shape, the crowd at your backs parts — and a robed figure pushes through, staff raised, voice already rising to gather listeners: a travelling preacher, drawn by the commotion, calling out that the bells are a sign, that any who follow you toward Saint Orrin's walk toward salvation, not doom. He's already drawing a following before you've taken ten steps.

The scene's central question — whether you can reach the belltower before the hive claims Tomas — now sends you out of Hollowmoot and onto the road to the temple. The plea has been answered; the party moves.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: I've sheltered with this pilgrim band three times through the years while working the Causeway tolls — they're faithful folk who called me 'sister' and shared their bread and water freely. Back then, I was just a river-girl reading the marshes for safer passage. But that was before I took the Order's bell-lore and made myself marked. If any of them know my face now, know what I've done, they'll see me as a heretic and thief, and the old kindness will curdle into fear.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: Your songs carry far in this swamp, pilgrims, and I know that's dangerous — but people are being called into darkness by the bells, and I need to know what you've seen at the temple. I'm staying with you, even if it means slow.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra accepts the compel on 'A Pilgrim Band'.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: Brack found them years ago—old coins and weathered bone near a half-collapsed weir-gate in the deep marsh. When Yarrow investigated, he discovered a water-stained entry in his family's oldest map-case, his great-grandfather's hand marking a cache of "crown-sealed wages" hidden before the drowning. It's real enough that Yarrow can't dismiss it, and real enough that others will believe.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: "I found what I found years back, and I'm not fool enough to lead anyone to a grave in these waters. You want to dig for old coin? Do it on your own time—but not with me, and not while folk are dying to the blight."

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow accepts the compel on 'Rumor of Buried Treasure'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: Shelter at the pilgrim band's crowded camp huddled beneath the sunken pilgrim's gate, dozens packed shoulder to shoulder for the safety of numbers hides a whispered rumor of hidden silver buried somewhere in the reliquary crypt, passed pilgrim to pilgrim until half the camp believes it.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Beneath the sunken pilgrim's gate the camp is a press of wet bodies and low hymn-murmur, dozens huddled under oilcloth for warmth they don't quite have. A woman with a scarred lip clutches Petra's sleeve — "Sister, is it true, is it true what they're saying?" — and around the fire-rings the same whisper keeps circling: silver in the reliquary crypt, enough to buy a family off this drowning road forever. Someone's already sharpening a boat-hook that has no business being sharpened. Yarrow feels eyes on him too — Brack growls low at a stranger who's been asking a few too many questions about weir-gates and old maps. Outside the gate's broken arch, rain sheets down, and somewhere under it, a Warden patrol works its slow way down the shoreline with torches lit.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: You know me—three times I've sheltered with you, eaten your bread. The bells are singing people into the dark, and greed is just another hunger. Stand with me, not for silver, but for the faith that's kept us alive.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra tears her arm from the scarred-lip woman's grip and steps into the firelight. Her voice cuts through the whisper-circle of treasure-talk, clear and hard. She speaks of the bell-song and the calling, of people drowning to the blight while the camp hungers for coins. She invokes her own years with them—the shelter they gave freely, the bread shared when there was nothing—and appeals to the bonds that have kept them breathing. If that kindness dies now for silver, then they're already drowned.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: The bells called Tomas by name—I need to know if anyone else heard themselves called, or if anyone here came from the temple with marks or wounds. Did the swarm-song touch any of you before you fled?

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm moves quietly through the crowded press of wet bodies beneath the sunken gate, his eyes methodically scanning each face and hand for the pale threading of hive-touch beneath the skin, the tremor in fingers, the thousand-yard stare of someone still listening to something no one else can hear. He keeps his voice low and steady, working closer to Mabel and the others, asking his questions with the careful urgency of a man who knows how fast the blight spreads through wounds.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: I've brought babes into worse storms than fear. Listen to me—stay quiet, stay calm, and you get off this drowning road alive.

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock stands with the weight of a midwife's authority and moves through the crowded camp, catching the sharpener's eye, then Mabel's, then the whisper-carriers around the fire-rings. She plants herself between the blade and the desperate, speaking firmly but soft—loud enough to steady them, not loud enough for the Wardens to hear.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: No one's digging anything tonight. Wardens are out there, and anyone who lets greed pull their eyes from the storm is volunteering to die to the bell-song.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow stands, Brack pressing tight against his side, and steps into the firelight where someone's sharpening that boat-hook. His eyes sweep the camp—reading the fear underneath the hunger, the way desperation turns good folk cunning and cruel. When he speaks, his voice is steady as a line of posts: the voice of someone who's held a line before and knows what breaks it. He plants himself between the fire and the reliquary entrance, calm and immovable.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra — create advantage with Rapport: dice + + - -, invoking shares scant bread [PX-05] → Superb (+5) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Caddock — create advantage with Empathy: dice 0 - 0 -, invoking Unshakeable calm in any birth, any storm [CA-04] → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow — overcome with Notice: dice + 0 0 + → Fantastic (+6) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Petra's words land like a struck bell — the scarred-lip woman lets go, shamefaced, and around the fire-rings the treasure-whisper dies mid-breath as the crowd remembers her three winters of shared bread. From the press of bodies a gaunt, wild-eyed man rises — a travelling preacher who's been sheltering here, drawing his own small flock with talk of hidden sin — and he seizes the moment, striding to stand beside Petra, lending his voice to hers: "The sister speaks true! Repent your greed, or the swarm-song claims you same as the temple's dead!" It works almost too well; Caddock, moving quiet as a midwife's hand, eases the boat-hook from the sharpener's grip before anyone notices, and the camp settles into wary, watchful calm — Pilgrims Heeding Caddock's Calm now sits as solid as the ground beneath the sunken gate. Yarrow, Brack pressed hard against his leg, reads every face in the firelight and finds what he needs: no informants here, no eyes reporting to Wardens, only frightened people who now trust the party more than the rumor. Mabel the pilgrim elder finally steps forward once the fire's gone quiet, her voice dropping to something private. "Tomas's grandfather isn't the only one — we've lost three since the rains worsened. The belltower calls its own, and it calls by name, sister, same as it called yours." She looks hard at Petra. "You said you hear it too. Watch yourself in there." Outside, the Warden patrol's torchlight slides past the broken arch and does not stop. The night settles into an uneasy truce: shelter held, information paid for, the road to Saint Orrin's now clear ahead.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: I sheltered him years back when the blight took his daughter—burned it out of her myself with herbs and ritual, refused his coin, only asked he remember the debt. I thought that bought loyalty. When the Drowned Priest's people came with their own coin and promises, he folded. Fear and silver loosened what gratitude had tied together.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: The innkeeper traded an old debt for whatever salvation the Drowned Priest's followers offered. That's what drowning men do—they'll cling to any hand that reaches down, even a hive-rotten one.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Anselm accepts the compel on 'A Weary Innkeeper'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: the Drowned Priest's acolytes seizes the party's goal at The goal is seized at the Weary Innkeeper's dry common room — the one dry room in flooded Hollowmoot where half the town, including your party, has been sheltering supplies and whispered plans. using The Drowned Priest's fanatical acolytes flood in through the common room's side door at his signal, moving as one body, singing low, and simply take what they came for before anyone can stop them..

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The side door of the common room bangs wide on its wet hinges and they're already inside — a dozen soaked figures moving as one, humming low under their breath in a rhythm that isn't quite the swarm-song but isn't far from it either. The Weary Innkeeper stands frozen by his own hearth, rag still in hand, not meeting anyone's eyes as the acolytes sweep past him toward the stores and the crate of relics you'd hidden beneath the floorboards. Refugees scatter from the benches, someone's soup kettle goes over with a clatter, and at the heart of the huddle a woman in a rain-slick grey shawl lifts her chin and starts to sing louder, drowning out every voice in the room but her own. Whatever you do next, you have maybe a dozen heartbeats before they're out the door and gone into the flood-dark lanes with it.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: That's not a bell—that's a lie! And I'm stopping you!

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra cuts through the scattered refugees toward the woman in grey, homing in with the certainty of someone who's heard every true bell-song ever rung. The false rhythm grates against her ear instantly—she sees the flaw, the moment where the chantress's concentration falters. She reaches for the woman's arm, moves to wrench her away from the relics and the other acolytes, ready to throw her bodily toward the door if it takes that to shatter the spell.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: The true rite speaks! Your song is hollow!

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm steps forward into the common room chaos, his voice rising to meet the Chantress's hive-song. He speaks the old liturgy of Saint Orrin - the exorcism words that once burned the blight from flesh and bone - throwing his deep knowledge of those rites against her corrupted melody as a counter, trying to shatter the dark harmony holding the acolytes together as one body.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: The blight falls back from flame and smoke—I'll choke it out of this room!

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock moves to the common room's hearth in quick, purposeful strides. She grabs kindling and cloth, feeding them to the flames with practiced efficiency, then uses her considerable strength to sweep her arm through the rising smoke, sending billows of ash and acrid fog toward the advancing acolytes in thick, choking clouds.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: Not while I'm standing here—I've held worse and I'll hold this too!

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow steps into their path with the trained bearing of a militia guard, driving at the Acolyte Chantress to physically break her song and disrupt the acolytes' coordination before they reach the hidden relics.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra — attack with Notice: dice + + 0 - → Superb (+5) vs Great (+4): SUCCESS (Acolyte Chantress stress 1)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Anselm — attack with Lore: dice - 0 + -, invoking Knows the old exorcism rites of Saint Orrin [AN-03] → Superb (+5) vs Great (+4): SUCCESS (Acolyte Chantress stress 2)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Caddock — create advantage with Crafts: dice + + 0 0 → Superb (+5) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow — attack with Physique: dice 0 0 - +, invoking Brack warns him before the hive-touched strike [YA-02], Recoils From Smoke and Fire [H-02] → Epic (+7) vs Superb (+5): SUCCESS (Acolyte Chantress mild consequence)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Acolyte Chantress attacks Petra (mental): Average (+1) vs Petra's Will Good (+3) — defended

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The common room becomes a wall of noise and smoke and violence, and the Chantress cannot hold the center of it. Petra's grip wrenches the false rhythm out of her throat mid-note, the swarm-song fracturing into a ragged cough; Anselm's old liturgy rides over the wreckage of her hymn like a bell drowning a whisper, and when Yarrow's shoulder drives into the huddle of acolytes, the shrieking retaliation the Chantress aims at Petra's oldest fear goes wide — Petra hears her own name in the hive's mouth and does not flinch this time. Caddock's hearth-smoke rolls thick and acrid through the room, and the acolytes recoil from it exactly as blight-touched things do, coughing, stumbling, losing whatever unity the song gave them. By the time the haze clears, the Chantress is on one knee coughing blood-flecked spit onto the floorboards, her flock scattering out the side door empty-handed into the rain, and the relic crate under the floorboards is still there, untouched. The Weary Innkeeper finally looks up from his hearth, rag forgotten in his hand, shame plain on his face as the last acolyte vanishes into the dark — the debt he sold is a debt he'll have to live with now.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Water sheets down the broken clerestory as you push past the reliquary screen, the acolytes' hymn still ringing in your ears from the inn. Ahead the stair spirals up out of the flood, dry for the first time in eleven years, and at its top the Drowned Priest waits in the belltower with the bell-rope wound around one fist like a noose. The swarm-song is not distant anymore — it comes from here, from him, from whatever the bell is calling down through the water. Below you the temple groans, stones shifting where the flood has eaten the mortar, and somewhere in the dark a boy's voice — Tomas's, maybe — answers the song in kind.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: Tomas, climb! The song is lying to you!

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra bolts up the spiral stair, two steps at a time. Stone cracks beneath her feet as the temple shudders, but she doesn't slow—she hears what the priest is doing to the bell, twisting her vow into a lure. She reaches the belltower, breath sharp, and lunges for the bell-rope wound around his fist.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: The song is lies! Tomas, hear the true words—the words that bind and cleanse! The bell was never meant to call souls into the water—it was meant to keep the darkness *out*!

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm's voice cuts through the flooded temple, ancient and precise. He's studied the remains of Saint Orrin's exorcism rites for years, and in this moment he sees it whole—the swarm-song is a twisted inversion of those sacred words, their solemn cadence perverted into a siren-call to the deep. He plants his feet on the staircase and shouts the true counter-phrases, each word a bell-strike against the false harmony, seeking to shatter the song's grip on the boy before he reaches the belltower.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: Tomas! My voice, not the bells! Come to me!

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock moves up the spiral stair toward Tomas's voice, her unshakeable calm cutting through the swamp-song's pull as she climbs toward the belltower. The steady presence of a midwife who's guided people through worse than any bell or shadow.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: Not Tomas—not while I draw breath. Your song ends here.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow charges up the spiral stairs, muscles straining against the swarm-song's pressure, closing on the Drowned Priest with the grim determination of a guard who will not abandon the line. The bell-rope and the priest's wild eyes are all that matter now.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra — attack with Athletics: dice + - + 0, invoking Knows Saint Orrin's bell-patterns by heart [PE-03] → Fantastic (+6) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (The Drowned Priest stress 3)

transcript.text: Anselm — create advantage with Lore: dice - - 0 0, invoking Knows the old exorcism rites of Saint Orrin [AN-03], Reads the ruined liturgy others can't [AN-03] → Fantastic (+6) vs Superb (+5): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Caddock — overcome with Empathy: dice - - 0 0, invoking Unshakeable calm in any birth, any storm [CA-04], Reputation as the finest midwife in the Sallowmere [CA-04], Steady hands that never falter under pressure [CA-04] → Epic (+7) vs Fantastic (+6): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow — attack with Physique: dice 0 + 0 +, invoking Loyalty that never wavers, dog or man [YA-02], Stubborn tracker who never loses a trail [YA-03] → Beyond Legendary (+9) vs Fantastic (+6): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (The Drowned Priest mild consequence)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: The Drowned Priest attacks Yarrow (physical): Great (+4) vs Yarrow's Athletics Average (+1) — hit for 3

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Petra's fingers close on the bell-rope just as the Priest tries to wrench it free, and Anselm's true liturgy slams into the swarm-song like a hammer on cracked glass — the false rhythm shatters mid-note, and up in the dark Tomas's answering hum stutters, breaks, turns to a boy's frightened sob. Caddock is already there, arms open, steady voice cutting through the ringing silence where the song used to be, and the boy stumbles into her without a fight left in him. Yarrow takes the clapper's iron kiss across his ribs and doesn't go down, planting himself between the Priest and the stair as stone dust sifts from a widening crack overhead. The Drowned Priest reels back against the bell-frame, bleeding, robes soaked black, the rope torn from his grip — and with the temple groaning its last warning around him, he throws himself through the shattered louvre into the flood below rather than be taken, vanishing into the black water with a wet, thrashing splash. The swarm-song is gone. Only rain, and Tomas's ragged breathing, and the slow terrible creak of Saint Orrin's giving way beneath you all.

An old temple sexton, half-crushed when the nave floor gave way beneath him, drags himself into Hollowmoot on a makeshift crutch — the stones buried three of his fellow pilgrims and he alone crawled free.
He begs you to go to Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple, where the bells still ring out over the flood and pilgrims still answer their call no matter who they bury.

costs.tag: Freezes when the song calls her name
costs.text: As she presses the sexton for the exact route, the swarm-song rises again beneath the rain and Petra hears her own name woven through it — she has to fight to keep her voice steady while everyone waits on her for direction.

As you try to settle into the crowded pilgrim camp for shelter, the band's loud hymn-singing and shuffling, slow-moving mass makes it impossible to move quietly or quickly — and worse, the noise carries straight toward anything listening for it.

Word of the buried silver has already turned ugly: a knot of pilgrims-turned-prospectors, whispering hidden silver among themselves, corners Yarrow and demands he lead them to it, treasure hunters turning violent when he hesitates to answer.
The goal is seized at the Weary Innkeeper's dry common room — the one dry room in flooded Hollowmoot where half the town, including your party, has been sheltering supplies and whispered plans.
The Drowned Priest's fanatical acolytes flood in through the common room's side door at his signal, moving as one body, singing low, and simply take what they came for before anyone can stop them.

The innkeeper always Sells Out Lodgers when the coin is good enough — true to that old habit, he'd already whispered word of what the party carried and sought to the Drowned Priest's people, and that's exactly how the acolytes knew where and when to strike.
